The itviec_active_jobs and itviec_active_job_skills views provide jobs and skills after moderation filtering for the dashboard’s job list, KPIs and charts. itviec_deleted_jobs and itviec_moderation_control_v3 help identify jobs to exclude from public results.

Vietnam IT Job Market collects IT job listings from ITviec, processes them with Python, stores Parquet on S3 and analyzes the data using Athena/Streamlit. This workshop explains component setup and AWS operation.

Component Processing current Upsert by job_id, preserve first_seen and update last_seen history NEW/UPDATED Record new jobs or changed fields UNCHANGED Count in the summary without creating a separate event EXPIRED A valid source deadline has passed; reason EXPLICIT_SOURCE_DEADLINE A job does not expire automatically because it is absent from discovery. ACTIVE/EXPIRED are record states, whereas history contains events; event counts therefore need not equal job counts.
Open staged/current/itviec/currentjobs.json and staged/history/itviec/events*.json within the same run directory to trace job_id values and the summary.
Track Jobs Across Synchronization Runs first_seen preserves the time a job was first recorded, while last_seen stores its most recent observation. These fields track the same job across collection runs without losing its original observation time. status represents the job’s state in the current dataset.
Data Change History The history file records new, updated and expired job events for each synchronization run. summary aggregates the processing results; each event includes the job ID, change type and event time. Unchanged jobs are counted in the summary without creating separate events.
Check the results Current data stores job information after synchronization; history stores events generated during the same processing run.

title: Project Proposal
content:
VIETNAM IT JOB MARKET Building an AWS platform for collecting, processing and analyzing IT recruitment data 1. Project summary This proposal presents the Vietnam IT Job Market solution and summarizes its actual implementation results.
Vietnam IT Job Market collects and analyzes IT recruitment listings from ITviec. The project covers collection, cleaning, storage, querying and presentation on a website. Users can explore recruitment demand within the dataset, find suitable jobs, save listings and track their applications.
Python runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance to collect and process data. Analytical Parquet files are published to Amazon S3; AWS Glue Data Catalog defines their metadata, and Amazon Athena queries them. Streamlit and Plotly provide the website through Nginx and HTTPS. DynamoDB stores moderation state and administrative audit records; S3 stores accounts and personal activity.
The goal is an AWS data processing and web application system with scheduled updates and operational monitoring. Its data covers ITviec listings only and does not represent the entire Vietnamese IT job market.
2. Problem and practical needs Recruitment listings span multiple detail pages, vary in presentation and change over time. Reading each listing is inefficient when comparing skills, employers, locations or experience requirements. Repeated collection also introduces duplicate URLs, changed content and expired listings, affecting statistics unless handled consistently.
Job seekers need a place to save opportunities and record application progress. Administrators need to moderate displayed listings, monitor data and identify operational issues.
The project addresses these needs through a consistent data pipeline, analytical dashboard, personal features and administrative tools on one website.
3. Objectives and scope Implementation objectives Collect ITviec URLs and job details, check duplicates and store JSON data. Synchronize current data and change history, normalize fields and export analytical Parquet. Connect S3, Glue Data Catalog and Athena to the dashboard. Display KPIs, charts, search, filters and job details. Provide registration, login, personal features and USER/ADMIN authorization. Support soft deletion, restoration and moderation auditing. Deploy on EC2 with HTTPS, automate the pipeline and centralize logs in CloudWatch. Users User group Supported needs Visitors View market summaries, filter and search listings USER Save jobs, track applications and manage a personal profile ADMIN Manage users, moderate listings and monitor system health Application tracking records progress entered by the user. Applications are submitted through the original ITviec link; the system neither sends CVs automatically nor synchronizes recruitment outcomes from ITviec.
4. Solution architecture The main resources are deployed in Asia Pacific (Singapore), ap-southeast-1. One EC2 instance runs the pipeline, dashboard and workers. Storage, query and monitoring services work together as follows:
Component Purpose Amazon EC2 Runs Python Collector/ETL, Streamlit, Nginx and workers Amazon S3 Stores analytical Parquet, Athena results, user data, moderation snapshots and deployment packages AWS Glue Data Catalog Stores table names, column schemas and data locations for Athena Amazon Athena Queries S3 recruitment data for the website Amazon DynamoDB Stores soft deletion, restoration and moderation audit records AWS IAM Grants EC2 resource access through its Instance Role AWS Systems Manager Provides server administration and inspection through Session Manager Amazon CloudWatch Centralizes logs and monitors pipeline failure alarms Streamlit and Plotly Provide the interface and interactive charts Nginx and Certbot Provide reverse proxy, HTTPS and certificate maintenance Data flow: ITviec → Python collection and processing on EC2 → Parquet on Amazon S3 → Amazon Athena → Streamlit Dashboard. AWS Glue Data Catalog supplies table schemas and data locations to Athena.
Moderation flow: ADMIN action on the website → state and audit stored in DynamoDB → Projection Worker exports a snapshot to S3 → Athena filters soft-deleted jobs.
5. Implementation 5.1. Collection and processing The collector discovers URLs from ITviec listing pages, normalizes links and removes duplicates before collecting details in batches. JSON output includes information for tracking each run.
Synchronization uses job identifiers to update current data and record changes. Observation timestamps track listings across updates. Collection completeness is checked before handling missing listings, so collection gaps are not mistaken for expired jobs.
ETL cleans and normalizes titles, companies, locations, skills, experience, levels and salaries. Undisclosed salary information remains missing rather than being estimated. Output is exported to Parquet with a consistent schema.
5.2. Analytical storage and queries Raw, current, history and clean JSON are processed on EC2. Analytical Parquet is published to analytics/itviec/current_jobs.parquet on S3. Run artifacts are stored separately for inspection and traceability.
Glue Data Catalog provides metadata for database vn_it_job_market and source table itviec_current_jobs. Athena queries this data and application views. Separating analytical data from artifacts prevents reading multiple versions of the same dataset.
5.3. Dashboard and job search The dashboard shows active jobs, employers, salary disclosure and skills. Charts cover posting trends, requested skills, locations, employers, experience, levels and salary disclosure. Weekly comparisons show changes between two periods.
Users can combine keywords with location, level, experience, company and salary filters. KPIs, charts and listings update with the selected filters. Job details include recruitment information and the original ITviec link.
5.4. Accounts and administration The website supports email registration and login with USER/ADMIN authorization. Accounts and personal activity are stored on S3. Users can save or unsave jobs, update application status, edit their display name and introduction, and change their password.
ADMIN pages cover System status, User management, Job management and Data quality. Soft deletion changes visibility while retaining source data for restoration. DynamoDB stores moderation state and audit records; the Projection Worker synchronizes a snapshot to S3 for Athena filtering.
5.5. Deployment and operations CloudFormation manages EC2 infrastructure. The recorded configuration uses a t3.small instance, 30 GiB gp3 EBS and an IAM Role for application AWS access. Streamlit runs in a Linux Python environment managed by systemd.
Nginx accepts web traffic, terminates HTTPS and proxies HTTP/WebSocket to Streamlit at 127.0.0.1:8501. The Security Group opens ports 80 and 443 for web access. Certbot and a timer maintain HTTPS for the server’s public IP address.
A systemd timer schedules the pipeline at 02:00 Vietnam time daily. Catch-up handling covers missed schedules; the Operations Worker handles permitted recovery requests. CloudWatch Agent and a journal exporter send service logs to CloudWatch.
6. Data protection and reliability S3 Block Public Access limits unintended public exposure; SSE-S3 encrypts stored data. The application uses IAM permissions granted to its runtime. HTTPS protects traffic between the browser and website.
Authorization is checked in administrative operations. DynamoDB stores moderation state and audit records in the same transaction to keep deletion and restoration consistent with the audit trail. Both tables have deletion protection and point-in-time recovery enabled.
CloudWatch retains logs in /vn-it-job-market/ec2 for two weeks. The PipelineFailure metric filter detects FAILED in logs; its alarm uses a threshold of at least one occurrence within five minutes. Alarms are monitored in the Console; no email or other notification destination is configured.

title: Control record and moderation synchronization to S3
content:
Role in the system The view layer ensures that the dashboard uses only jobs eligible for display. The Projection Worker converts DynamoDB moderation state into an S3 snapshot for Athena filtering; job and skill views apply the same moderation state.
Configuration used The application uses DynamoDB as the primary moderation source. META#CONTROL contains state/revision information; the Projection Worker exports an S3 snapshot with schema_version=2 and backend=DYNAMODB for Athena.
Moderation control record META#CONTROL stores moderation backend control information, including the change revision and S3 snapshot synchronization settings. The application and Projection Worker use it to coordinate moderation updates between DynamoDB and the data read by Athena.
READY indicates that the moderation backend is ready according to the control record. revision tracks changes; projection_bucket and projection_prefix identify the S3 output location at control/moderation/. audit_table specifies the audit table.
Moderation snapshot on S3 control/moderation/ stores the moderation snapshot read by Athena. The Projection Worker reads DynamoDB state and exports it here, allowing analytical queries to apply administrators’ moderation decisions.
job_moderation.json supplies moderation data to Athena tables and views. The views use it to exclude soft-deleted jobs from public results.
The snapshot uses schema_version: 2 and backend: DYNAMODB to identify its structure and moderation source. revision allows comparison with DynamoDB; deleted_jobs supplies soft-deleted job IDs for Athena filtering. In this snapshot, revision is 0, and deleted_jobs and audit_log are empty.

PIPELINE_BUCKET=vn-it-job-market-data-381924757765-ap-southeast-1-an PIPELINE_PARQUET_KEY=analytics/itviec/current_jobs.parquet PIPELINE_PUBLISH=true Run the service after the previous run has finished:
sudo systemctl start --no-block vnjob-pipeline.service sudo journalctl -u vnjob-pipeline.service -n 120 --no-pager -o cat The runner processes or reuses discovery under the source conditions, validates the entire run, writes artifacts outside analytics, prepares the journal and backup, updates the canonical object using IfMatch with its ETag, and promotes local data. If the same Vietnam calendar day and mode already have a SUCCEEDED run, the runner records SKIPPED. Do not delete the marker to force a run.
Check the run’s status.json and S3 metadata:
sudo -u vnjob .venv/bin/python -c 'import boto3,json; d=boto3.client("s3",region_name="ap-southeast-1").head_object(Bucket="vn-it-job-market-data-381924757765-ap-southeast-1-an",Key="analytics/itviec/current_jobs.parquet"); print(json.dumps({k:d.get(k) for k in ("ETag","LastModified","Metadata")},default=str,indent=2))' SUCCEEDED and published=true must match the run-id and sha256 metadata. ETag is used for conditional writes and is not assumed to be SHA256. PIPELINE_PUBLISH=false may still process and commit local data; it is not a read-only mode.
Check the results The canonical object, artifacts and local state can be traced to the same run. On failure, retain the journal for recovery rather than forcing an overwrite.
Trace Published Data The run-id metadata links the Parquet file on S3 to the pipeline run that produced it. sha256 stores the content checksum for integrity verification. The object’s run-id in the screenshot matches the successful run recorded in Section 4.7.3.

title: Validate the Entire Collection Run Before ETL
content:
Run in: SSM on EC2
Objectives Pass only validated data to current-data synchronization.
Prerequisites The runner orchestrates all batches from one discovery file.
Procedure Monitor the journal and run status:
sudo journalctl -u vnjob-pipeline.service -n 120 --no-pager -o cat sudo systemctl status vnjob-pipeline.service --no-pager In data/runs/<RUN_ID_THUC_TE>/status.json, check stage, completed_batches, crawled, the final status and published. Read the file as vnjob or with the appropriate SSM permissions.
The runner validates the batch count, discovery_file, expected/success/failed counts, batch_complete and unique IDs across the complete dataset. It then writes validated_snapshot.json and runs sync, clean and export. Missing batches or errors prevent the input from passing ETL validation. Checkpoints keyed by the discovery SHA reuse URLs only within the limits implemented in the source.
Do not combine batches from different discovery files. For HTTP 403/429 responses, stop and assess source access conditions; do not retry continuously or lower coverage checks to force validation to pass.
Check the results The run has a run_id, valid aggregated input and an accurate final status. On failure, failed_stage and error_type identify the issue.
Run Results on 11 November 2026 Run 20261111T081952Z-a435a240 completed 25/25 batches, collected 624 jobs and finished with SUCCEEDED and published=true. After synchronization, current data, clean data and Parquet contained 1,072 records; the Parquet file had 24 columns. The current dataset includes previously stored records and updates from this run.

title: Feedback and suggestions
content:
This section contains my personal takeaways and perspectives — Nguyen Ngoc Lan, an Information Technology student in class K68CNTTB at Vietnam National University of Agriculture — after 12 weeks of participating in the First Cloud AI Journey program and the Vietnam IT Job Market project. The following assessments are written from the perspective of an IT student gradually turning theory into practical skills on the cloud computing platform.
Evaluation by aspect 1. Learning environment and methodology
Instead of cramming theory, the program guided us to approach AWS through practical hands-on labs. Applying the storage and processing of IT recruitment data into practice helped me deeply understand the nature of each service, rather than just memorizing their names. I learned the habit of carefully reading the documentation and checking configurations before hitting the “Deploy” button.
2. Documentation and support culture
The documentation system on Cloud Journey is logically organized and easy to look up when forgotten. Additionally, the program’s “ask right - answer direct” culture helped me practice my error description (debug) skills, providing the correct logs/error messages instead of asking vague questions. This is an extremely important technical communication skill for my future career.
3. Connection to specialized knowledge
The Vietnam IT Job Market project is a perfect demonstration of a real-world Data Pipeline: from running Python scripts to collect data on EC2, pushing Parquet files to S3, using Glue Data Catalog to define structures, to using Athena for querying. It helped me connect all the fragmented knowledge about networking, storage, and databases learned at school.
4. Most noticeably improved skills
The mindset of looking up specialized English documentation and understanding AWS system architecture. Carefulness and discipline when assigning IAM Roles and Security Groups to ensure security. The ability to read CloudWatch logs to independently isolate and troubleshoot issues. Skills in synthesizing, editing documents, and presenting technical reports visually and clearly (leveraging my personal strengths from media and union activities). Feedback questions What am I most satisfied with?
I am most proud of my progress in being able to independently operate the core components of a data system. Starting with a lot of confusion, I now clearly understand why S3 is used instead of a traditional Database for a Data Lake, or how to optimize a query on Athena. Having all results backed by logs or Query IDs helps me work with solid evidence and much more confidence.
What should the program improve?
Add short exchange sessions (mini-workshops) between internship groups to analyze different solutions for the same problem. Provide more documentation or checklists related to Cost Optimization right from the first labs, helping students form a mindset of saving cloud resources early on. Create a shared Knowledge Base compiling classic troubleshooting cases from previous cohorts for newcomers to easily reference. Would I recommend the program to friends?
Definitely yes. This is an ideal “combat” environment for proactive students who are not afraid to read English documentation and want to improve their independent problem-solving abilities.
Further suggestions and orientation Promote operational practice (Operations): I hope the program adds hypothetical scenarios (e.g., pipeline failing halfway, EC2 crashing) so interns can practice system recovery (Backup/Restore). Personal orientation: After the internship, I plan to continue delving into Python, Data Engineering, and Cloud Computing. I will further refine the visualization (Dashboard) for the Vietnam IT Job Market project and pursue additional AWS certifications to expand career opportunities. Acknowledgments
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the Mentors at AWS Vietnam, the First Cloud AI Journey community, and my fellow interns in the group. This 12-week journey not only equipped me with sharp technical knowledge but also helped me shape a more independent, professional, and responsible working mindset — an invaluable asset for my IT career ahead.
